land.text: Tabriz, where the Rawadids ruled as local lords of Azdi Arab ancestry under the Sajids (page: dynasty dates 900-1071)

predecessors.note: The page gives no founding event; 900 is its dynasty date. The first dated Rawadid ruler is Husayn I (955-988).

land.text: Azerbaijan: "The Seljuks under Tughril conquered the principality in 1054 CE"

successors.note: Mamlan II reigned 1058/9-1070 as a Seljuk vassal and Alp Arslan deposed him in 1071; the Maragha line of Ahmadil (c.1100-1116) and the Atabakane of Maragha (to 1227) continued.

capitals.name: Tabriz
capitals.note: The page: the dynasty "initially controlled Tabriz and north-eastern Azerbaijan"; Wahsudan also held Maragha and the Sahand strongholds. An earthquake devastated Tabriz in 1042-1043.

rulers.name: Abu'l-Hayja Husayn I
rulers.note: the page lists Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Rawadi before him, dates "? - c. 953?"

rulers.name: Abu Mansur Wahsudan
rulers.note: list gives 1025-1058/9 (the text elsewhere 1019-1054); defeated by Tughril in 1054, his son Mamlan taken

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Rawadid row): the dynasty "initially controlled Tabriz and north-eastern Azerbaijan". The page gives no area; the shape is Tabriz with a 60 km radius until the Sallarid page's 948 gain of the land northeast of Tabriz.

correction.text: Tabriz and the land northeast of it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "948: Marzuban was defeated and captured. The Rawadids took land northeast of Tabriz."

correction.text: Azerbaijan: Tabriz, Maragha, Ardabil and the Sahand

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 979 the Rawadids "conquered the lands of the Musafirid ruler Ibrahim I ibn Marzuban I"; the page says they ruled "Azerbaijan and parts of Armenia in the second half of the 10th and much of the 11th century" (the Armenian parts are undated and not drawn).

ledger.note: 900: the Rawadids hold Tabriz. The page dates the dynasty '900-1071' and says it 'initially controlled Tabriz and north-eastern Azerbaijan'; the Rawadids were Azdi Arabs who arrived in the mid-8th century and later became Kurdicized.

948: the Rawadids take land northeast of Tabriz. 'Marzuban was defeated and captured. The Rawadids took land northeast of Tabriz.' [Reviewer me-08-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the Sallarid page gives the Rawadid gain after its 948 entry, not in that year.]

region.text: Azerbaijan, the lands of the Musafirid ruler Ibrahim I ibn Marzuban

ledger.note: 979: the Rawadids conquer Sallarid Azerbaijan. 'Per Kasravi, the Rawadids conquered the lands of the Musafirid ruler Ibrahim I ibn Marzuban I' in Azerbaijan in 979 (Sallarid page: they 'overran much of the province around 979', and captured the last Sallarid holding, Marzuban b. Isma'il, in 984).

1054: Tughril conquers the Rawadid principality. 'The Seljuks under Tughril conquered the principality in 1054 CE.' Wahsudan was defeated and his son Mamlan taken; Mamlan II reigned 1058/9-1070 as a Seljuk vassal and Alp Arslan deposed him in 1071.
1054: the independent Rawadid principality ends with the Seljuk conquest (the page's dynasty dates run to 1071, the deposition of Mamlan II).

wars.name: Rawadid conquest of Sallarid Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Land northeast of Tabriz in 948, most of Azerbaijan around 979, the last Sallarid holding in 984.

wars.name: Oghuz crisis in Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Oghuz families fleeing Mahmud of Ghazni (1028) were settled by Wahsudan as vassals; he helped the Hadhbani Kurds defeat the Oghuz at Maragha in 1029, had Oghuz leaders killed at a dinner in 1040-1041 and was defeated by Turks in the Sarab desert in 1041-1042. No border moved.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of the Rawadids
wars.outcome: Tughril conquered the principality in 1054; Wahsudan was defeated and his son Mamlan taken.

certainty.note: A principality known by its cities (Tabriz, Maragha, Ardabil) and the Sahand strongholds; the pages give no frontiers.

notes: Cliopatria has no Rawadid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. No area on the page. The page's dynasty dates: header '900-1070/1116', body '(900-1071)'; the independent principality is taken to end with the 1054 Seljuk conquest (end 1054), after which Mamlan II (1058/9-1070) reigned under Seljuk suzerainty; the Seljuk dossiers should carry that vassalage. Ahmadil ibn Ibrahim ibn Wahsudan ruled Maragha c.1100-1116/7 (stabbed by Ismaili assassins in Baghdad) and his descendants ruled Maragha and Tabriz as the Atabakane of Maragha until the Mongol invasion in 1227: an 'Ahmadilis' dossier may be wanted (not written). Not on the page: Ganja (Wahsudan 'traveled there', no year), Arran, Dvin, the 984 capture, Moghan/Ardabil (a Mamlan II campaign, no year), the Armenian parts of the realm. Disagreements: Wahsudan 1025-1058/9 (list) vs 1019-1054 (text). Start 900 is the page's dynasty date, not a founding event; the first documented ruler is Husayn I (955). Gazetteer names needed: none (Tabriz and Azerbaijan provinces resolve).
